cohort: The study included 345 women aged 40 and over and 366 women under 40 who delivered between January 2015 and December 2024 at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Pregnancies in women aged 40 and above had significantly higher rates of cesarean section, preterm delivery, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and postpartum hemorrhage, but also a higher 5 min APGAR score and incidence of chromosomal abnormalities, compared to younger women.
mod_finding: Women aged 40 and over had significantly higher rates of cesarean section (73% vs. 36.1%, p < 0.0001) compared to women under 40.
